chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibrāhīm al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Ṣaghīr, from his grandfather Shuʿayb, from Mufaḍḍal, who said:
Were it not for the insistence of these Shiʿah upon Allah in seeking sustenance, He would have moved them from the condition in which they are to one more constricted than it.

key_terms.إِلْحَاحُ: earnest persistence and repeated entreaty in supplication
key_terms.الرِّزْقِ: sustenance, provision, and livelihood granted by Allah
key_terms.الشِّيعَةِ: the followers and adherents of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, the One to whom supplication for provision is directed
key_terms.الْحَالِ: the present state or condition a person is in

ai.seo_question: How does persistent du'a affect a believer's sustenance according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the persistent du'a of the Shiʿah to Allah for rizq is a cause for relief and protection from greater hardship. It highlights both the importance of turning to Allah in seeking livelihood and the reality that sustenance is under His control.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Al Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Sagheer, from his grandfather Shuayb, from Mufazzal who said,

‘Had these Shias not pleaded to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding seeking of the sustenance, He<sup>azwj</sup> would have Transferred them from the state which they are in to what is more constricted than it’.
en.sarwar: 16. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim al-Hadhdha’ from Muhammad ibn Saghir from his grandfather, Shu’ayb from Mufaddal who has said the following: “
has said, ‘Had it not been for this Shi’a’s (followers) insistence on receiving more sustenance from Allah He would have moved them from their present condition to a more severe poverty.”
